etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: First attested in 1622. From Italian ingraziare or Medieval Latin *ingratiatus, from Latin in grātiam (“for the favor of”).
senses: (reflexive) To bring oneself into favour with someone by flattering or trying to please them; to insinuate oneself; to worm one's way in.
(followed by to) To recommend; to render easy or agreeable.
